what_its_for: Vigabatrin is a seizure medicine (anticonvulsant). It is used to treat a type of severe infantile spasms (also called West syndrome) in babies 1 month to 2 years old. It is also used together with other medicines to control complex partial seizures in adults and children 10 years and older whose seizures have not been controlled by other treatments. It works by calming overactive nerve signals in the brain that cause seizures.
how_to_take: Take vigabatrin exactly as your doctor tells you. It comes as a tablet or as a powder packet that you mix with water. If using the powder packet, mix the entire contents of the packet with 10 mL of cool or room temperature water and stir until fully dissolved. The liquid should be clear. Use an oral syringe to measure and give the right dose. You can take vigabatrin with or without food. Swallow tablets whole with water. Do not crush or chew the tablets unless your doctor says it is okay. Take it at the same times every day to keep steady levels in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your age, weight, and how well your seizures are controlled. Do NOT change your dose or stop taking it without talking to your doctor first — stopping suddenly can make seizures worse. For infantile spasms in babies, the usual starting dose is 50 mg/kg/day given in 2 divided doses. For adults with partial seizures, the usual starting dose is 500 mg twice a day, which may be slowly increased up to 1,500 mg twice a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store tablets and unopened powder packets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. Once you mix the powder with water, use it right away — do not save the mixed liquid for later. Keep all medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush medicines down the toilet or pour them down the drain. Ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do activities that require alertness until you know how vigabatrin affects you, because it can cause dizziness and drowsiness. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Do not stop taking vigabatrin suddenly without your doctor's approval. Tell all of your doctors and dentist that you take this medicine before any procedure or surgery.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: sudden changes in your vision, blurry vision, or tunnel vision (seeing only straight ahead but not to the sides) — this is a serious side effect that can cause permanent vision loss; new or worsening depression, anxiety, or thoughts of hurting yourself; feeling very confused, agitated, or having unusual behavior changes; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or trouble breathing; worsening seizures or new types of seizures; unusual eye movements (especially in babies); extreme sleepiness or weakness; numbness or tingling in your arms or legs. IMPORTANT WARNING: Vigabatrin can cause permanent vision loss (loss of side/peripheral vision). Your vision MUST be tested before starting this medicine, and regularly while you take it. Tell your doctor immediately if you notice any changes in your vision.
when_it_works: Vigabatrin may start to reduce seizures within a few days to a few weeks after you begin taking it. For infantile spasms, improvement is often seen within 2 to 4 weeks. For partial seizures in adults, it may take several weeks to see the full benefit. Keep taking your medicine as directed even if you feel well. Do not stop on your own — your doctor will monitor how well the medicine is working and adjust your dose if needed.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Vigabatrin may harm an unborn baby. However, uncontrolled seizures during pregnancy can also be dangerous. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. BREASTFEEDING: Vigabatrin passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. BABIES AND CHILDREN: Vigabatrin is approved for use in infants with infantile spasms and children 10 and older with partial seizures. Babies must have their eyes checked regularly by an eye doctor. ELDERLY: Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially dizziness, drowsiness, and vision problems. Dose adjustments may be needed. KIDNEY PROBLEMS: If you have kidney disease, your doctor may need to lower your dose, since vigabatrin is removed from the body through the kidneys.
